s: A company has an application that generates reports and stores them in an Amazon S3 bucket When a user accesses their report, the application generates a signed URL to allow the user to download the report. The company's security team has discovered that the files are public and that anyone can download them without authentication The company has suspended the generation of new reports until the problem is resolved. Which set of actions will immediately remediate the security issue without impacting the application's normal workflow?
o: Create an AWS Lambda function that applies a deny all policy for users who are not authenticated. Create a scheduled event to invoke the Lambda function
Review the AWS Trusted Advisor bucket permissions check and implement the recommended actions.
Run a script that puts a private ACL on all of the objects in the bucket.
Use the Block Public Access feature in Amazon S3 to set the IgnorePublicAcls option to TRUE on the bucket.

w.y: The objects are public through ACLs, and the fix must be immediate without breaking the signed-URL download flow. Setting Block Public Access IgnorePublicAcls on the bucket makes S3 ignore all public ACLs at once, including those on existing objects. Presigned URLs keep working because they are authorized by the signer's IAM credentials.

o.A: Lambda can't apply a 'deny unauthenticated users' policy on a schedule; this is slow, indirect and not immediate.
o.B: Trusted Advisor only flags the problem; it doesn't fix it immediately.
o.C: Rewriting ACLs object by object takes time on large buckets and doesn't protect new objects written with public ACLs.
o.D: Correct: IgnorePublicAcls takes effect immediately for all objects, and presigned URLs still work.
